title: Legacy Archive Synthesis for Historical Research
business: Academic research institutions managing digitized historical document repositories.
problem: Researchers struggle to synthesize insights from massive, fragmented document sets due to the high cost and complexity of manual cross-referencing across 150k-word archives.
solution: Utilizing the 200K token context window of Claude Sonnet 4.5 to ingest entire document collections in a single pass, allowing the model to perform thematic extraction and cross-document synthesis without needing complex RAG orchestration.
steps: Aggregate historical document batches into a single text-based context block.
Initialize the API request using the claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 model ID.
Define a system prompt that mandates extended thinking to analyze thematic overlaps.
Execute the request within the 200K token limit to generate a unified research summary.
Archive the output and prepare for migration to newer models before the November 2026 retirement date.
outcome: Researchers achieve a cohesive, multi-document narrative synthesis that maintains semantic consistency across the entire provided archive.
limitation: The model has a fixed knowledge cutoff of January 2025; users must verify if recent historical interpretations or metadata updates are required by checking the model's output against external, post-cutoff scholarly databases.
